title: I Took the Sousaphone-Bell Checkout to the Drum Major Who Left My Numbered Bits

parts.text: I stepped into the band cage at 3:03 p.m. and drum major Vic was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE BELL. FORTY-FIVE MINUTES. BITS STAY WITH THE CHECKOUT. I was twenty-five, band secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered bits. Vic shrugged. "Majors are the bell." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover mouthpiece on my numbered bits. Then I asked for the bell log. At 3:11 the cage pinged why Vic's name was on my bits. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The cage can see Vic's leftover mouthpiece on my numbered bits.

social.video_title: He left my numbered sousaphone bits on my checkout — Part 1/2
social.description: Band cage, leftover mouthpiece, a forty-five-minute clock he posted. I logged the bits. Would you have asked for the bell log?

parts.text: Vic called it lip slurs until the cage asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the mouthpiece still. The bits went back to my numbered checkout. Vic ran a slot of his own and told the next major atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MAJORS ARE NOT THE BELL. I keep my bits in a labeled pouch. Vic brown-bags his slurs. The cage finally looks like a checkout, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Majors are not the bell — Part 2/2
social.description: Bell log, numbered bits, and a second line on the board. Was a lip slur ever my mouthpiece?
